fullPassage: While there is live debate among philosophers about whether understanding is itself a kind of knowledge, it is generally agreed that understanding is something beyond mere knowledge of facts. To illustrate the plausibility of this idea, consider a student who simply parrots what their biology teacher tells them. This student knows, for example, that the DNA sequences of humans and chimpanzees are extraordinarily similar because the teacher has said this. However, the student may be clueless as to why this is so, or the importance of this similarity within the larger context of biology. The student may have no grasp of how this fact provides support for evolution in general and common descent in particular. What is missing? It seems that whereas the student simply knows these isolated facts, understanding requires seeing how these facts hang together. The person with understanding grasps biology as an interrelated body of information with many connections between the various facts. This person can appreciate how these various facts depend upon one another. Furthermore, the person who understands biology can use this understanding to explain and sometimes predict particular biological phenomena.

questions.stem:
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

While there is live debate among philosophers about whether understanding is itself a kind of knowledge, it is generally agreed that understanding is something beyond mere knowledge of facts.

(A) What is missing? It seems that whereas the student simply knows these isolated facts, understanding requires seeing how these facts hang together.

(B) To illustrate the plausibility of this idea, consider a student who simply parrots what their biology teacher tells them. This student knows, for example, that the DNA sequences of humans and chimpanzees are extraordinarily similar because the teacher has said this.

(C) However, the student may be clueless as to why this is so, or the importance of this similarity within the larger context of biology. The student may have no grasp of how this fact provides support for evolution in general and common descent in particular.

det.korean: (B)-(C)-(A): 도입 → 예시 → 한계 → 결론
det.analysis:
✅ ③ (B)-(C)-(A): (B)에서 this idea를 받아 예시 제시(앵무새 학생) → (C)에서 However로 학생의 한계 설명(이유 모름) → (A)에서 What is missing?으로 귀결(고립된 사실 vs 이해) ←정답

❌ ① (A)-(B)-(C): (A)의 What is missing?이 먼저 오면 앞에 학생 예시가 없어 맥락 단절
❌ ② (A)-(C)-(B): (A) 후 However(C)는 대조 대상 없음
❌ ④ (C)-(A)-(B): (C)의 However가 첫 단락이면 대조 대상 없음
det.tip: this idea(도입) → 예시(B) → 한계 However(C) → 결론 What is missing?(A)

questions.passage: While there is live debate among philosophers about whether understanding is itself a kind of knowledge, it is generally agreed that understanding is something beyond mere knowledge of facts. To illustrate the plausibility of this idea, consider a student who simply parrots what their biology teacher tells them. This student knows, for example, that the DNA sequences of humans and chimpanzees are extraordinarily similar because the teacher has said this. However, the student may be clueless as to why this is so, or the importance of this similarity within the larger context of biology. The student may have no grasp of how this fact provides support for evolution in general and common descent in particular. What is missing? It seems that whereas the student simply knows <u>these isolated facts</u>, understanding requires seeing how these facts hang together. The person with understanding grasps biology as an interrelated body of information with many connections between the various facts. This person can appreciate how these various facts depend upon one another. Furthermore, the person who understands biology can use this understanding to explain and sometimes predict particular biological phenomena.
